title: Text In, Text Out: The Limit

questions.question: Without tools, llama3.2 replied 'The support ticket ID is #TS-001.' What actually happened?
options: Nothing: the model generated likely text that claims an action
The model called a hidden tool
questions.explanation: A model only outputs text. Claims of actions without a tool call are inventions.

questions.question: Which of these needs a tool rather than a better model?
questions.explanation: Fresh data isn't in the weights or the prompt.

questions.question: In one tool round trip, what does the model return on the first turn?
options: A tool call: the tool's name and arguments
questions.explanation: Your code runs the tool, then the model answers from the result on the next turn.

questions.question: In the live run, how often did llama3.2 choose the right tool?
questions.explanation: Choosing was easy; the failures came after the tool returned.

questions.question: With no tools in the final request, the model said 'The status I provided earlier was fictional.' Why?
options: llama3.2's template only adds 'use the tool output' guidance when tools are in the request, so it misread the result
questions.explanation: Sending the tool definitions on the final turn too raised the score from 3/6 to 5/6.

questions.question: Evaluating the action question in two conditions created two tickets. What does that imply?
options: Tests and evals of side-effecting tools have real effects; use fakes, sandboxes or idempotency
questions.explanation: Lessons 7 and 11 cover making side effects safe to test.
